## Overview

This project predicts residential sale prices using property characteristics and location. Starting from 20,000 housing records, I created features for sale year and month, age at sale, time since renovation, renovation status, and basement presence. ZIP codes were one-hot encoded so the model could learn location-specific price patterns.

## Model and results

I trained an `XGBRegressor` with 800 trees, a 0.05 learning rate, and maximum tree depth of 6. On a held-out 15% test set, it achieved:

| Metric | Result |
|---|---:|
| Test RMSE | **$101,498.41** |
| R² | **0.9223** |
| Training RMSE | $46,214.86 |

The gap between training and test RMSE is a useful reminder that strong predictive performance can still coexist with some overfitting, especially in a flexible gradient-boosting model.

## Analysis

The notebook also examines feature importance and breaks down RMSE across price bands. These checks make the model easier to interpret and help identify where its errors are largest.

The complete feature engineering, modeling, evaluation, and holdout prediction workflow is available in the [house-price-prediction project folder](https://github.com/ooheap/owen-heap-portfolio/tree/main/projects/house-price-prediction).
